brief.headline: Jensen Confirms Three-Supplier HBM4 Race; Samsung-SK Gap Tightens Post-Broadcom Selloff
brief.summary: <cite index="4-1,4-12,4-13,4-14">Jensen Huang landed in Seoul on June 5 and confirmed Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron are all qualified and in production for HBM4 delivery to Vera Rubin shipping Q3 2026.</cite> <cite index="20-1,23-2,23-6">Samsung closed down 6.4% and SK Hynix plunged 9.92% on June 5 following Broadcom's weak AI guidance, wiping ~20% from 2x leveraged ETFs.</cite> <cite index="10-2,10-7">DRAM contract pricing surged 90-95% QoQ in Q1 and is forecast to rise another 58-63% in Q2, while NAND jumped 55-60% in Q1 with 70-75% projected for Q2.</cite> <cite index="4-16,4-17">Industry analysts estimate SK hynix holds 60-70% of HBM4 volume allocated to Vera Rubin, with Samsung at 25-30% and Micron the remainder, reflecting SK hynix's 62% overall HBM market share as of mid-2025.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="22-3,22-5">SK hynix's market cap reached 93.2% of Samsung Electronics' as of May 31, up from 46.5% a year ago, with YTD gains of 258.4% vs 164.4% respectively.</cite> <cite index="4-19,4-20">Samsung was first to begin HBM4 mass production on Feb 12 using a 4nm logic die reaching 3.3 TB/s and has shipped HBM4E samples targeting 3.6 TB/s for Vera Rubin Ultra in 2027.</cite> <cite index="1-11,1-12,1-17">SK hynix holds 62% HBM shipment share as of Q2 2025 and is projected to capture ~70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026.</cite> Tactical read: Friday's selloff leveled the field after SK's outperformance, but Samsung's HBM4E lead and foundry optionality offer hedged exposure if HBM allocation narrows. SK remains the purer HBM play with higher beta to memory ASP upside. Relative value hinges on Q2 HBM3E pricing discipline and M15X fab ramp visibility.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-1,13-6">Q1 2026 DRAM contract pricing surged 90-95% QoQ (revised from initial 55-60% forecast), while NAND rose 55-60% (from 33-38%).</cite> <cite index="10-7,10-9">Q2 projections call for 58-63% DRAM and 70-75% NAND QoQ increases, driven by capacity reallocation to AI-related applications and limited client supply.</cite> <cite index="11-5,11-7,11-25">Samsung and SK Hynix signal no aggressive capacity expansion; HBM's 3-to-1 consumption ratio vs DDR5 is compressing general-purpose memory supply, with pricing rally projected to extend past 2028.</cite> <cite index="11-22,31-3">Hyperscaler capex exceeds $600B in 2026 (40% YoY), with ~$450B directed to AI infrastructure.</cite> Suppliers prioritizing profitability over volume; new fab capacity unlikely before late 2027.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-1,4-13,4-14,4-15">Jensen Huang confirmed all three vendors—Samsung, SK hynix, Micron—are qualified, in production, and racing to support Vera Rubin for Q3 2026 ship.</cite> <cite index="3-6,3-1">HBM3E will account for 66% of total HBM output in 2026, down from 87% in 2025 but still the clear majority.</cite> <cite index="3-11,3-15">Nvidia recently asked suppliers if they could deliver 16-layer HBM in Q4 2026, pulling forward the generational transition before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full commercial rollout.</cite> <cite index="6-2,6-12,6-13">HBM3E supply remains tight as Samsung and SK hynix prioritize HBM4 ramp; 2026 HBM revenue mix forecast ~55% HBM4, 45% HBM3E, with HBM4 absorbing demand from Q3.</cite> <cite index="4-4,4-5,4-8">HBM4 delivers 2 TB/s bandwidth per stack at JEDEC baseline; Samsung's production HBM4 reaches 3.3 TB/s using a 4nm logic die, while each Vera Rubin NVL72 rack carries 1.6 PB/s aggregate bandwidth.</cite> <cite index="2-5,2-6">SK hynix's Cheongju M15X fab clean room completes May 2026 with pilot operations starting; facility will manufacture both HBM3E and HBM4 with 10nm-class 1c DRAM for HBM4E.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: Jensen Huang confirms all three HBM4 suppliers qualified for Vera Rubin Q3 ship
news_pulse.implication: Eliminates binary Samsung qualification risk; shifts focus to allocation splits (SK 60-70%, Samsung 25-30%, Micron remainder). Broadens HBM supply base and validates Samsung's Feb 12 mass production start.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix plunge 6.4% and 9.92% on Broadcom-led chip selloff
news_pulse.implication: Profit-taking after YTD rally (Samsung +164%, SK +258%). 2x leveraged ETFs down 20%, triggering negative compounding for retail. Sentiment reset, not fundamental deterioration—HBM demand intact.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM prices revised to +90-95% QoQ in Q1, +58-63% forecast for Q2
news_pulse.implication: Sequential upward revisions (original Q1 forecast: 55-60%). Conventional DRAM ASP trajectory supports margin expansion through H2. Supply-demand gap widening across server, PC, mobile DRAM.

news_pulse.headline: NAND Flash contract pricing jumps 70-75% QoQ in Q2 after 55-60% Q1 surge
news_pulse.implication: NAND outpacing DRAM for first time in cycle; enterprise SSD demand absorbing capacity. Samsung/SK reallocating NAND lines to DRAM. Client SSD/eMMC lowest priority, capacity crunch extends to late 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia signals interest in 16-layer HBM delivery by Q4 2026
news_pulse.implication: Accelerates transition before 12-layer HBM4 matures. Suppliers begin internal planning; 16-layer likely classified HBM4 or HBM4E. SK hynix developing hybrid bonding as backup; Samsung focusing on hybrid bonding early.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex raised to $700-725B, up 60%+ from 2025
news_pulse.implication: Meta raised 2026 capex to $125-145B; Amazon ~$200B; Alphabet $175-185B; Microsoft $110-120B. 75% directed to AI infrastructure. Supply-constrained environment sustains memory pricing power; demand visibility through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity targeted at 130k wafers/month by end-2026, doubling from late 2024
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS-L enables 12-16 HBM4 stacks for Rubin. Nvidia secured >60% of 2025-26 capacity. CoWoS bottleneck easing but still gating factor for AI accelerator shipments. Arizona CoWoS/3D-IC targeted before 2029.

news_pulse.headline: SK hynix market cap reaches 93.2% of Samsung, triggering bubble warnings
news_pulse.implication: Hana Securities warns reversal could signal bull market top, citing 2000 Cisco/MSFT analog. Counterargument: Samsung 2026E net profit 280T won vs SK 208T won supports fundamentals. Concentration risk elevated.

brief.derivatives_signal: 2x leveraged ETFs hit historic lows post-selloff; KODEX/TIGER SK Hynix products down 20% in single session, triggering negative compounding. Retail net-bought ₩585B in leveraged products during decline (Samsung ₩191B, SK ₩395B), suggesting capitulation incomplete. Implied vol spike creates tactical entry for long gamma into M15X ramp catalysts and Q2 earnings (late July). Monitor basis between KRX spot and OTC ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) for overnight sentiment shifts.
